source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug should be at the bedside of a client on pyridostigmine for myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: Atropine is kept available for cholinergic crisis from cholinesterase inhibitor overdose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors (PDF p. 111)
questions.quote: Keep Atropine sulfate available for overdosage (cholinergic crisis)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When is pyridostigmine best given for myasthenia gravis?
questions.rationale: It is given 30–60 minutes before meals so muscle strength peaks for chewing and swallowing, with some food for gastric upset.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Acetylcholinesterase Inhibitors (PDF p. 111)
questions.quote: Administer medication 30 minutes to 1 hour before meals.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When is suicide risk HIGHEST in a client starting antidepressants?
questions.rationale: Suicide precautions are maintained especially as depression lifts and energy returns.
questions.quote: Maintain suicide precautions especially as depression lifts.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When are SSRIs and TCAs usually given?
questions.rationale: SSRIs can cause insomnia, so they are given in the morning; TCAs cause drowsiness, so at bedtime.
questions.quote: Give SSRI in morning, TCAs at bedtime.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: How long may antidepressants take to show effect?
questions.rationale: Effects may take 2 to 4 weeks; clients are taught not to stop early.
questions.quote: Effect of medication may take up to 2 to 4 weeks

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which food is AVOIDED by a client on an MAO inhibitor?
questions.rationale: Tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, beer, wine, chocolate) can cause hypertensive crisis with MAOIs.
questions.quote: Hypertensive crisis with ingestion of foods high in tyramine (beer, wine, chocolate)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug treats MAOI hypertensive crisis per the handout?
questions.rationale: Phentolamine is given in MAOI hypertensive crisis.
questions.quote: Give Phentolamine in case of hypertensive crisis.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which is an early sign of lithium toxicity?
questions.rationale: Toxicity signs include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle weakness, and confusion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Stabilizers (PDF p. 112)
questions.quote: Toxicity signs: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, weak muscles, confusion

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which teaching is correct for a client on lithium?
questions.rationale: Adequate fluids and normal sodium prevent lithium retention and toxicity; take with meals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mood Stabilizers (PDF p. 112)
questions.quote: High intake of fluids and normal sodium

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on haloperidol has involuntary lip-smacking and tongue movements. What is this?
questions.rationale: Tardive dyskinesia is a late EPS with involuntary oral-facial movements.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which teaching applies to a client on chlorpromazine?
questions.rationale: Antipsychotics cause photosensitivity; avoid sunlight, alcohol, and hazardous activities.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.rationale: Atypicals (CROQZ): clozapine, risperidone, olanzapine, quetiapine, ziprasidone.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which teaching applies to benzodiazepines such as diazepam?
questions.rationale: Benzodiazepines are never stopped abruptly; alcohol potentiates them.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which condition contraindicates anxiolytics like benzodiazepines?
questions.rationale: Contraindications include hypersensitivity, acute narrow-angle glaucoma, and liver disease.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After spinal anesthesia, how long is the client kept flat to prevent headache?
questions.rationale: Keep the client flat 6–12 hours after spinal anesthesia to prevent spinal headache.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Local Anesthetics (PDF p. 115)
questions.quote: SPINAL ANESTHESIA: keep the client flat for 6-12 hours to prevent spinal headache.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which peripheral muscle relaxant facilitates endotracheal intubation?
questions.rationale: Peripheral relaxants such as succinylcholine block the myoneural junction for intubation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skeletal Muscle Relaxants (PDF p. 116)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which is a serious risk of COX-2 inhibitors like celecoxib?
questions.rationale: COX-2 inhibitors carry risks of MI and stroke, plus nephrotoxicity.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which teaching applies to a client on allopurinol for gout?
questions.rationale: Increase fluids to prevent renal calculi; avoid high-purine foods and fermented drinks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Anti-Gout Agents (PDF p. 117)
questions.quote: Increase OH to prevent renal calculi

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Ondansetron belongs to which class of antiemetics?
questions.rationale: Ondansetron and granisetron are serotonin (5-HT3) antagonists.
